Use case: identity-preserve. Game portrait animation sheet, exactly FOUR COLUMNS and TWO ROWS, overall wide 3:1 composition, no text or margins. Each cell is a 3:2 chest-up frame, exactly aligned. Reference is the existing fictional normal weathered commentator looking down over a railing. Preserve his identity, ordinary human proportions, receding tousled gray-dark hair, short gray beard, cheap headset, forward lean and DOWNWARD eyes. He watches the field BELOW the screen from a balcony. No upward gaze, no looking at camera, no heroic jawline.
Requested changes: replace olive overshirt with a short-sleeved HAWAIIAN SHIRT, muted faded brick-red with large cream and moss-green palm-leaf shapes, worn over dark tee, believable casually rumpled clothing. Skin natural gray-beige, colors dirty and desaturated, dim ordinary broadcast booth light. Increase pixel block size DRAMATICALLY: human anatomy derived from candid PHOTO pixelization, roughly 96x64 logical pixels PER CELL enlarged with nearest neighbor, clear large square clusters, 3-4 skin shades. No detailed high-resolution painting, no smooth gradients, no comic outline, no glamorous game mascot, no grinning caricature. Faces normal and rough.
All frames plain almost-black background. Thin rough dark wooden balcony rail horizontally across bottom of each cell. Body fully within each cell.
Column 1: absorbed observation, chin lowered 25 degrees, eyes down-right, shoulders relaxed, forearms on rail.
Column 2: modest enthusiasm, small authentic smile, eyes still DOWN, one low hand gesture.
Column 3: tense furrowed brow, looking further down, one hand on headset.
Column 4: urgent commentary, leaning forward more, eyes DOWN, one hand on rail.
TOP ROW: mouths CLOSED in natural pause, corresponding four expressions.
BOTTOM ROW: EXACT corresponding same four frames, identical body/head/hands/pixel placement, ONLY mouth/jaw slightly open for natural speaking. Column4 mouth open wider for shout, still realistic no comedy mouth.
Precise matched mouth animation pairs vertically, no labels, no panels, no borders, no logos. This is a production sprite atlas, not concept art with titles.

Use case: stylized-concept. Game portrait animation sheet of an ORIGINAL fictional French-speaking technical sports analyst named VALLIN, not a portrait or caricature of any real broadcaster. Exactly FOUR COLUMNS TWO ROWS, wide overall 3:1, each cell 3:2 chest-up, no labels/text/borders/margins.
Middle-aged ordinary nerdy man, lean face, receding neatly combed dark-gray hair, small old-fashioned rectangular spectacles, clean-shaven, cream collared shirt under worn charcoal-brown cardigan, narrow dark tie slightly loosened, cheap black broadcast headset and mic. Human and restrained, not cute, not cartoon, not sinister. Slight air of professional dignity and dry amusement. Forearms resting on plain thin dark wooden commentary-booth railing at bottom of each cell, small notebook or pencil only in lower hands. Leans forward and looks DOWN-LEFT toward the playing field below screen, chin lowered around25degrees, eyes NEVER at camera and NEVER up. His face is photo-derived natural human anatomy rendered in VERY COARSE nearest-neighbor pixel art, approx96x64 logical pixels each frame. Large visible square pixels, 4 skin tones, broad clusters, muted desaturated gray-beige skin and dark fabric, dim practical light, almost-black flat background. No smooth painting, no fine dithering or glossy rimlight. Matches a rough ordinary pixelized photograph.
Four columns: 1 concentrated neutral; 2 one eyebrow raised with faint skeptical half-smile; 3 very intent on the result with hand adjusting spectacles; 4 dry amused aside toward fellow presenter just to his left while still glancing down. Natural restrained range, not exaggerated.
TOP ROW all4 mouths CLOSED in pause. BOTTOM ROW EXACT same four head/body/hand poses and framing, ONLY mouth slightly open mid-explanation. Perfect vertical animation pairs, same sizes and alignment. No text, no titles, no marks.
